notes: Take the head, keep the elements equal to it, ask whether that is the whole list, then turn the flag into 0/1 by counting the evidence list. The `[ drop ] dip` picks the head and closes a segment.

program: quote [ 1 sub ] dip swap cons swap [ quote ] map [ [ lt? ] cat ] map [ quote ] map swap [ cat ] swap cons map [ uncons filter ] map [ [ drop 1 ] map ] map [ 0 [ add ] fold ] map [ 1 sub ] map
notes: code = (number of thresholds in (lo-1, hi) below x) - 1: each x becomes the predicate (x lt?) with the thresholds catted behind it, `uncons filter` keeps the thresholds below x, then count and subtract one. Assumes lo <= hi+1 (the sampler draws lo < hi); no zip needed.

program: [ swap ] dip over sub quote [ 0 lt? ] filter 0 [ add ] fold add [ over swap sub ] dip swap quote [ 0 lt? ] filter 0 [ add ] fold add sub quote [ 0 lt? ] filter 0 [ sub ] fold
notes: Uses min(0,v) as `quote [ 0 lt? ] filter 0 [ add ] fold` instead of 9-op iftes: min(hi1,hi2) = hi1 + min(0, hi2-hi1), max(lo1,lo2) = lo1 - min(0, lo1-lo2), and the answer is -min(0, max - min) via a `0 [ sub ] fold`.

program: [ nil quote dup cat ] dip [ quote ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map [ [ cons cons ] cat ] map swap [ i uncons quote cat ] fold uncons [ uncons swap drop ] dip [ [ sub ] swap cons ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map swap [ i quote cat ] fold dup [ 0 swap sub ] map cat [ 0 lt? ] filter 0 [ sub ] fold
notes: Each x becomes the closure (uncons x cons cons) and a fold with body `i uncons quote cat` deals the list into first-of-pair and second-of-pair buckets; the second bucket becomes closures (uncons b sub) and a fold `i quote cat` zips out the signed gaps; the total of |g| is minus the sum of the negatives among the gaps and their negations. Brute force found no 4-atom single-body bucket toggle, hence the closures.

program: dup 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold swap [ nil quote dup cat ] dip [ quote ] map [ [ uncons ] swap cat ] map [ [ cons cons ] cat ] map swap [ i uncons quote cat ] fold [ 0 [ add ] fold ] map [ dup add ] map swap [ div ] swap cons map
notes: Count the flat values n, deal the list into x and y buckets with the same closure fold as pair_gap_total, sum each bucket, double the sums and divide by n (floor(2s/n) = floor(s/k) since n = 2k).
